title: Multi-Stop Route Planner: Up to 30 Stops
description: Route up to 30 stops with a per-leg breakdown using the Multi-Stop Route Planner — total road distance and time for the whole round. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a nine-stop delivery round returns nine legs and a total — the day's skeleton, measurable before the van leaves the yard.
quick_answer: The Multi-Stop Route Planner routes a journey through up to 30 stops in your order, along real roads, and breaks it into legs with total distance and time. Add the stops, reorder them freely, and read the round as a whole before committing the day to it.

faq: This planner routes the order you give it, faithfully. Reordering to cut distance is the Route Optimizer's job — the two are designed to be used in sequence.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Leg times are network estimates; the day's real traffic is the day's own surprise.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Legs follow roads between stops. The total is the driven round, not the geometry of the dots.
Can route results change over time?
Road data improves and roads change; re-run a standing round each season rather than trusting an old total.
How many stops can I add?
Up to 30 — enough for a full delivery round or a very ambitious Saturday.
Can the route start and end at the same place?
Yes — add the depot as both first and last stop and the round closes on itself.
The roadbook and GPX tools elsewhere on the site cover documents and devices; this page's craft is the routed round itself.
Yes — a hub visited morning and evening is two stops. The leg table treats each visit as its own row, which is the day's truth.
What if two stops share an address?
Keep both if the visits are genuinely separate; delete one if it was a typing echo. The planner routes what it is given.
